# DraftEditor

A draft a person and an agent write together. In its growing text box the agent's words are highlighted in place, and a line above it says the agent wrote some of it and where the draft stands ("Needs your input", "Ready for your review", "Approved"). The person edits freely; `onValueChange` gives the new text and the runs updated to match, so what they type is theirs and what they leave keeps its author. Screen readers hear the agent's words in the box's description. An agent can ask for input or say the draft is ready for review, but only a person approves it: an `approved` shows only with a person in `readinessBy`.

```tsx
import { DraftEditor } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/draft-editor/draft-editor";
```

## Example

```tsx
<DraftEditor
  label="Reply"
  value={draft.text}
  segments={draft.segments}
  onValueChange={(text, segments) => setDraft({ text, segments })}
  readiness="ready-for-review"
  readinessBy={{ author: "agent", name: "Ouro" }}
  actions={<Button>Send</Button>}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `TextArea` instead for text only one person writes, and `DraftReview` to accept or reject an agent's changes one by one.

## Props

The props the modes share. Type: `DraftEditorProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `actions` | `ReactNode` |  | A send button and other actions, at the end of the box. |
| `agentLabel` | `string` | `"Written by an agent"` | The legend for the agent's highlight, for other languages. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: width, margins, grid placement (`mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | What the draft is, for screen readers ("Reply"). The box shows `placeholder` instead. Required. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `10` | Rows the box grows to before it scrolls. |
| `onValueChange` (required) | `(value: string, segments: DraftSegment[] \| undefined) => void` |  | Called when the person edits, with the new text and the runs updated to match: the person's typing is theirs, and what they did not touch keeps its author. Store both. The runs are `undefined` when `segments` did not join to `value`, since who wrote what is then unknown. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Text shown while the draft is empty. |
| `readinessLabel` | `string` |  | The readiness badge's text, for other languages. Defaults to "Needs your input", "Ready for your review" or "Approved". |
| `readinessNote` | `string` |  | A short note from whoever set the readiness ("Check the dates"). |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLTextAreaElement>` |  | The `<textarea>`. |
| `rows` | `number` | `2` | Rows the box starts with; it grows with the text. |
| `segments` (required) | `readonly DraftSegment[]` |  | Who wrote which part of `value`. Agent-written runs are highlighted in place. |
| `value` (required) | `string` |  | The draft's text (controlled). |

## Modes

`DraftEditorProps` is a union: pass the props of exactly one mode. Mixing them is a type error.

### Approved: `DraftEditorApprovedProps`

Approved by a person, named in `readinessBy`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readiness` (required) | `"approved"` |  | Where the draft stands, shown as a badge above it. |
| `readinessBy` (required) | `DraftReadinessBy & { author: "human" }` |  | The person who approved it. |

### In progress: `DraftEditorInProgressProps`

Drafting, needing input or ready for review, as a person or an agent says.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `readiness` | `"drafting" \| "needs-input" \| "ready-for-review"` | `"drafting"`, which shows the badge only once it moves on | Where the draft stands, shown as a badge above it. |
| `readinessBy` | `DraftReadinessBy` |  | Who set the readiness. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` and `TextareaHTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `defaultValue`: Not a prop. The draft is controlled: `<DraftEditor value={text} onValueChange={save}>`.
- `onChange`: Not a prop. `onValueChange` gives the text and the updated runs: `onValueChange={(text, segments) => save(text, segments)}`.
- `provenance`: Not a prop. The runs are `segments`: `<DraftEditor segments={segments}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: DraftEditor merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `DraftAuthor`

Who wrote a run of text: the person using the app, or an agent working with them.

```ts
type DraftAuthor = "human" | "agent";
```

### `DraftReadinessBy`

Who set the readiness: their kind, so a person's approval is told apart from an agent's, and the name to show.

```ts
interface DraftReadinessBy {
  /** A person or an agent. */
  author: DraftAuthor;
  /** The name to show ("You", "Ouro"). */
  name: string;
}
```

### `DraftSegment`

A run of the draft written by one author. The runs, joined, are the draft's `value`.

```ts
interface DraftSegment {
  /** Who wrote this run. */
  author: DraftAuthor;
  /** The run's text. */
  text: string;
}
```
